response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(DISTINCT e.ID) AS cnt FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), s AS (SELECT SEX, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share, AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM c) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess FROM s WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Examinations are inner-joined to Patient, so examinations with no matching patient are dropped. Blank and NULL SEX values form their own groups (NULL via GROUP BY).

The combined count is the sum of the per-sex distinct-patient counts. Each patient has one sex, so this equals the total number of distinct examined patients. The per-sex average is the mean of the counts across sex groups.
